summary.text: Andy Biggs is the U.S. Representative for Arizona's 5th District, seeking the governorship with running mate Sine Kerr, a former state senator. He previously served in the Arizona House and Senate, including as Senate President, and chaired the House Freedom Caucus for two years.

paragraphs.text: Biggs is an Arizona native who received a B.A. in Asian Studies from Brigham Young University, an M.A. in political science from Arizona State University and a J.D. from the University of Arizona.
He is a retired attorney who has been licensed to practice in Arizona, Washington and New Mexico.
Biggs served eight years in the Arizona House of Representatives and six years in the Arizona Senate, where he was elected Senate President in 2012.
He was elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and chaired the House Freedom Caucus from 2019 through 2021.

In Congress he chairs the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Federal Government Surveillance, sits on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, and co-chairs the Border Security Caucus.
Biggs and his wife, Cindy, have lived in Gilbert for more than 35 years and have six children and twelve grandchildren.

sources.title: Arizona Republicans choose Rep. Andy Biggs to challenge Gov. Hobbs
